I want to thank @ricardoalcantara for putting together a very thoughtful PR, which I have spent a lot of time reviewing. I also appreciate all the feedback from others and that Ricardo is actively incorporating those recommendations into this PR.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> The purpose of this initial review from me is to understand and evaluate the changes, and make any recommendations, if necessary, to follow Godot's guidelines. Others are actively running the changes on their visionOS hardware, which will be sufficient (from my perspective) to validate it is working.

For anyone else who comes along to read my review, I've noted my observations here.

At a high-level, I want to acknowledge that whilst the PR and changes seem extensive, I will share my observations in the following sections.

## Introduce the concept of an "Apple embedded" device

Many of Apple's hardware platforms share a lot of common code with iOS and its SDKs. This resulted in a large number of files being moved from `platform/ios` to `drivers/apple_embedded`. This change follows a similar convention established for other shared "drivers".

Only the platform-specific changes now live in their respective `platform/<name>` directories, and follow the same conventions as all the other platforms. 

✅ This refactoring is extremely valuable, as it will simplify adding tvOS in the future, should that happen.
 
## Exclude MetalFX temporal upscaling from the `servers` code. 

All the changes to the shared `servers` source was to update preprocessor definitions to exclude MetalFX temporal upscaling from visionOS. None of these changes affect non-Apple platforms, besides ensuring MetalFX continues to remain excluded.

✅ The details are being worked out; however, I expect we'll settle on something like `MFX_TEMPORAL_ENABLED` to avoid having to change it again in the future.

## Introduce less ambiguity to the iOS platform exporter code

Once again, as the Apple team has introduced "embedded" as a shared platform, it makes sense to update the exporter APIs to reflect this. 

✅ The changes rename a number of APIs from using `ios` to `apple_embedded`, and leave the existing as `deprecated`, to ensure backwards compatibility.

## Add the visionOS platform

These changes include additions for the project template, platform-specific runtime code for visionOS and additional APIs and exporter implementations for visionOS.

Almost exclusively additions, which make up a large number of files to support adding a new platform. This is not unexpected and would be the same for the consoles (which we don't see in open source) and any other platforms that may be supported in the future.

✅ Expected additions when adding a new platform.

## Metal Driver changes

Only a couple SDK availability changes, due to visionOS being much newer – there were no changes that will affect the existing macOS or iOS platforms.

## Final thoughts

I don't have any additional recommendations, as others have made the suggestions I would have considered, such as improving how we exclude MetalFX Temporal. 

We will need to validate iOS it is unaffected by the changes.

I've reviewed all code. Great PR! Adding iOS derived platform is much easier and cleaner than before.

I successfully export and run the [platform3d](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/3d/platformer) sample on my AVP. It launchs fine with both Forward+ and Mobile renderer. Audio and graphics works fine.

But my controller does not work as expected. I connect my PS5 controller to AVP through blue tooth. The sample does not respond to my joystick movement. I'm sure my hardware is correctly setup, as it works fine with other games on AVP, and the system UI can trigger click event when I press 'X' on the controller. 

I think controller support can be addressed in later PRs. This PR is already huge.

> Also considering AVP's performance, I think it's fine to use PC renderering defaults (Forward+, higher shadowmap resolution). That's something can be improved in the future, but out of scope of this PR.

This is the start of some incredible work, thanks @rsanchezsaez!

I was able to successfully export, build and deploy a visionOS app (joypads) and verify:

- ✅ App runs on visionOS natively
- ✅ Connected Xbox controller
- ✅ Verified controller works with Godot
- ✅ Verified rumble works with Godot

I look forward to testing a few more apps, but I am very satisfied it is ready!

I haven't done as an extensive review as Stuart, my skills are best suited once the immersive XR and volume changes are brought in.

Did get the platform 3D demo working on the AVP, very cool indeed.

My only remark is that the full export seems to be broken and thus remote debug doesn't seem to support visionOS but after talking to Stuart and Ricardo the consensus seems to be that this is not related to this PR but a broader problem.

As Stuart has remarked that he's willing to spend some of his time in diving into this deeper and fixing any build issues, I'm happy to see this PR merged from my end.

We still need buy-in from the iOS platforms guys (cc @bruvzg ) but my personal opinion is that we should move forward with this. I'm really looking forward to the more XR focussed additions.

I reviewed the code mostly with an eye for: code style and maintainability, architecture, buildsystem, thirdparty, documentation, compatibility.

Overall it looks great to me!

I pointed out a few things which should IMO be addressed before merging (marked as "[BUG]" or "[BUG?]"), and a bunch more things which are mostly code style / quality / maintainability improvements, which could be done in a follow-up, or here, as you prefer.

Looks great to me.

Amazing work @rsanchezsaez and everyone involved!
